Title: DeepLog: Anomaly Detection and Diagnosis from System Logs through Deep Learning
Authors: Min Du, Feifei Li, Guineng Zheng, Vivek Srikumar
Research_Problem: Anomaly detection in system logs is manual and time-consuming.
Method: LSTM-based sequential anomaly detection.
Main_Result: Achieved F1-score of 0.96 on HDFS.
Limitation: Lacks explainability for individual predictions.
Relevance: Provides a baseline for temporal sequence modeling of logs.

Title: AIOps: Real-World Challenges and Research Innovations
Authors: Qingwei Lin, Hongyu Zhang, Jian-Guang Lou, Yu Zhang, Xuanzhe Liu
Research_Problem: Cloud operations generate too much telemetry data for manual review.
Method: Survey of machine learning applied to IT operations (AIOps).
Main_Result: Identified key research areas including RCA and anomaly detection.
Limitation: High-level overview without specific model architectures.
Relevance: Highlights the need for self-healing and intelligent platforms.

Title: LogAnomaly: Unsupervised Detection of Sequential Anomalies Using Deep Learning
Authors: Weibin Meng, Ying Liu, Yichen Zhu, Shenglin Zhang, Dan Pei, Yuqing Liu, Yi-Chun Chen
Research_Problem: Log sequences have both quantitative and sequential anomalies.
Method: Template2Vec log representation with LSTM.
Main_Result: Outperformed DeepLog with 0.98 F1 on BGL.
Limitation: Does not provide human-readable root cause explanations.
Relevance: Demonstrates advanced log parsing and anomaly scoring.

Title: Why Should I Trust You?: Explaining the Predictions of Any Classifier
Authors: Marco Tulio Ribeiro, Sameer Singh, Carlos Guestrin
Research_Problem: Machine learning models act as black boxes lacking trust.
Method: LIME: Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations.
Main_Result: Demonstrated users trust models more when explanations are provided.
Limitation: Local explanations may not reflect global model behavior.
Relevance: Fundamental XAI method for explaining AI anomaly alerts.

Title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
Authors: Scott M. Lundberg, Su-In Lee
Research_Problem: Existing XAI methods lacked a unified theoretical foundation.
Method: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) based on game theory.
Main_Result: Provided consistent feature importance scores matching human intuition.
Limitation: High computational overhead for large neural networks.
Relevance: Core XAI technique — this project uses deterministic LR attribution instead.

Title: Robust Anomaly Detection for Multivariate Time Series through Stochastic Recurrent Neural Network
Authors: Ya Su, Youjian Zhao, Chenhao Niu, Rong Liu, Wei Sun, Dan Pei
Research_Problem: Multivariate cloud metrics have complex temporal dependencies.
Method: OmniAnomaly: Stochastic RNN with planar normalizing flows.
Main_Result: Achieved 0.89 F1 score on complex multivariate KPIs.
Limitation: Training is computationally intensive.
Relevance: Excellent method for predicting failures in temporal metrics.

Title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection via Variational Auto-Encoder for Seasonal KPIs in Web Applications
Authors: Haowen Xu, Wenxiao Chen, Nengwen Zhao, Zeyan Li, Jiahao Bu, Zhihan Li, Ying Liu, Youjian Zhao, Dan Pei
Research_Problem: Seasonal cloud KPIs are difficult to monitor for anomalies.
Method: Donut: VAE-based anomaly detection with MCMC imputation.
Main_Result: Achieved F1 of 0.75 to 0.9 on missing and seasonal data.
Limitation: Struggles with highly non-stationary data without seasonality.
Relevance: Addresses unsupervised detection of cloud metric failures.

Title: CloudRanger: Root Cause Identification for Cloud Native Systems
Authors: Ping Wang, Jialiang Sun, Haibin Wang, Jingyu Wang, Qi Qi, Jianxin Liao
Research_Problem: Root cause analysis is challenging in complex microservices.
Method: Dynamic causal graphs and random walk for RCA.
Main_Result: Identified root causes with high accuracy across microservices.
Limitation: Depends on complete tracing data.
Relevance: Crucial for the self-healing and RCA components.

Title: InterFusion: Interacting Hidden Dynamics and Macroscopic Observations for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
Authors: Zhihan Li, Youjian Zhao, Jiaqi Han, Ya Su, Rui Jiao, Xidao Wen, Dan Pei
Research_Problem: Time series metrics exhibit complex inter-metric dependencies.
Method: Hierarchical VAE capturing inter-metric and temporal dynamics.
Main_Result: Outperformed OmniAnomaly with 0.93 F1 score.
Limitation: Complex to tune hyper-parameters.
Relevance: Advanced failure prediction for cloud multi-metrics.

Title: Artificial Intelligence for IT Operations (AIOps) on Cloud Platforms
Authors: Jasmin Bogatinovski, Sasho Nedelkoski, Jorge Cardoso, Odej Kao
Research_Problem: Lack of structured overview of AIOps in cloud environments.
Method: Survey combining anomaly detection, RCA, and remediation.
Main_Result: Provided structured taxonomy of AIOps techniques and open challenges.
Limitation: Does not evaluate individual techniques experimentally.
Relevance: Directly aligns with the integrated AIOps platform goal.

Title: A Survey on Explainable Anomaly Detection
Authors: Zhiyuan Li, Yanfeng Shu, Yanru Gong, Youjian Zhao
Research_Problem: Fragmentation in XAI techniques applied to anomaly detection.
Method: Taxonomy and systematic review of XAI for anomaly detection.
Main_Result: Structured the field into feature-based, model-based, and post-hoc explanations.
Limitation: None (Survey).
Relevance: Provides theoretical background for selecting XAI techniques.

Title: Experience Report: System Log Analysis for Anomaly Detection
Authors: Shilin He, Jieming Zhu, Pinjia He, Michael R. Lyu
Research_Problem: Lack of comprehensive evaluation of log-based anomaly detection.
Method: Evaluated 6 classical ML models on system logs.
Main_Result: Found that simpler models often perform comparably to complex ones on specific logs.
Limitation: Only evaluated traditional models, not deep learning.
Relevance: Important baseline for cloud monitoring research.

Title: Seer: Leveraging Big Data to Navigate the Complexity of Cloud-based Debugging
Authors: Yu Gan, Yanqi Zhang, David Nguyen, Thana Mahindra, et al.
Research_Problem: QoS violations in microservices are hard to predict.
Method: Hardware-level telemetry + deep learning for QoS prediction.
Main_Result: Predicted QoS violations with 91% accuracy before they occur.
Limitation: Requires low-level hardware instrumentation.
Relevance: Key literature on predictive cloud failure prevention.

Title: DAGsHub: Self-Healing Cloud Microservices Using Advanced Fuzzy Logic
Authors: Areej Samir, Chinmaya Dehury, Piyush Harsh
Research_Problem: Microservices require automated self-healing to reduce downtime.
Method: Fuzzy-logic based self-healing with container autoscaling.
Main_Result: Reduced failure recovery time by 60% compared with manual intervention.
Limitation: Rule-based system; does not generalise to unseen failure types.
Relevance: Provides architectural precedent for autonomous cloud self-healing.

Title: Root Cause Analysis of Anomalies of Multitier Services in Public Clouds
Authors: Jia Weng, Jian Wang, Jianbin Yang, Yang Yang
Research_Problem: Multitier cloud services make root cause identification difficult.
Method: PC algorithm for causal discovery from metrics.
Main_Result: Accurately identified root cause tier in 85% of cases.
Limitation: Causal discovery scales poorly with many metrics.
Relevance: Relevant to the RCA phase of the autonomous system.

Title: A Systematic Literature Review of Cloud Monitoring Tools
Authors: Md. Mahbubul Islam, et al.
Research_Problem: Fragmentation in cloud monitoring tooling and approaches.
Method: Systematic literature review of 73 cloud monitoring papers.
Main_Result: Identified key gaps in predictive and autonomous monitoring.
Limitation: None (SLR).
Relevance: Motivates the need for intelligent predictive monitoring.

Title: Federated Machine Learning for Intelligent IoT via Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface
Authors: Kun Zhu, Wanli Ni, Yi Yang
Research_Problem: Distributed IoT/Cloud systems need lightweight predictive models.
Method: Federated learning with reconfigurable antenna communications.
Main_Result: Achieved strong model convergence with reduced communication overhead.
Limitation: Specific to federated/IoT settings.
Relevance: Demonstrates ML-based prediction for distributed infrastructure.

Title: Anomaly Detection and Classification using Distributed Tracing and Deep Learning
Authors: Sasho Nedelkoski, Jasmin Bogatinovski, Alexander Acker, Jorge Cardoso, Odej Kao
Research_Problem: Distributed traces contain complex patterns indicating anomalies.
Method: LSTM classifier on trace data.
Main_Result: Achieved 0.95 F1 for trace anomaly classification.
Limitation: Requires instrumented distributed tracing infrastructure.
Relevance: Relevant to temporal classification and microservice failure prediction.

Title: Causeinfer: Automated End-to-end Performance Diagnosis with Hierarchical Causality Graph in Large Distributed Systems
Authors: Jianping Chen, et al.
Research_Problem: Performance bottlenecks in distributed systems are hard to diagnose.
Method: Causality inference graphs from performance metrics.
Main_Result: Correctly identified root cause services in 82% of cases.
Limitation: Does not support real-time or automated remediation.
Relevance: Background for causality vs. correlation distinction in RCA.

Title: Detecting and Explaining Anomalies Caused by Web Tampering at the Edge
Authors: Meziantou Siddiqui, et al.
Research_Problem: Web edge infrastructure anomalies are hard to detect and explain.
Method: Lightweight ML + explanation at edge nodes.
Main_Result: Detected web tampering anomalies with <2ms latency.
Limitation: Specific to CDN/web edge context.
Relevance: Demonstrates lightweight explainable detection at infrastructure level.
